text:
### Customer Behavior  
**High-Risk Behavior:**
- Reluctance to provide documentation
- Vague about purpose of account
- Changes story about transaction purpose
- Uses third party as proxy
- Avoids using account normally after opening  
**Example:** Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it
name: Chunk 7/61

raw_entities.name: Reluctance to Provide Documentation
raw_entities.description: A customer exhibits unwillingness or resistance to supplying required identity, address, or beneficial ownership documentation during account opening or ongoing KYC verification. This is a key indicator of potential money laundering or account misuse.

raw_entities.name: Vague Account Purpose Statement
raw_entities.description: A customer is unable or unwilling to clearly articulate the legitimate business or personal purpose for opening or using the account. This vagueness prevents proper risk assessment and source of funds verification.

raw_entities.name: Inconsistent Transaction Purpose Narrative
raw_entities.description: A customer provides conflicting or changing explanations for the purpose or nature of transactions on their account. This inconsistency suggests potential deception or concealment of the true source or use of funds.

raw_entities.name: Third-Party Proxy Use for Account Activity
raw_entities.description: A customer uses another person as an intermediary or proxy to conduct transactions on their account rather than conducting transactions directly themselves. This arrangement may indicate structuring, layering, or an attempt to obscure the beneficial owner.

raw_entities.name: Dormancy Following Large Deposit
raw_entities.description: A customer opens an account, makes a significant deposit, but then fails to use the account for its stated purpose or for normal banking activity. This pattern is consistent with money laundering placement and layering techniques.
context: Avoids using account normally after opening
Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it

raw_entities.name: Large Deposit Followed by Third-Party Withdrawal
raw_entities.description: A customer deposits a substantial sum into a newly opened account and then immediately arranges for a third party to withdraw the funds. This pattern is a classic indicator of money laundering, structuring, or account misuse to obscure beneficial ownership and fund origins.
context: Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it

properties.description: Customer is unwilling or resistant to providing required documentation during account opening or verification processes
properties.required_action: Do not proceed with account opening; escalate to compliance team for review

properties.description: Customer provides unclear, evasive, or non-specific explanation of the intended purpose of the account
properties.required_action: Request clarification; do not open account until clear purpose is documented

properties.description: Customer provides conflicting or changing explanations for the purpose or nature of transactions
properties.required_action: Investigate discrepancies; document all versions of narrative; escalate if inconsistencies cannot be resolved

properties.name: Third-Party Proxy Use for Account Activity

properties.description: Customer uses a third party to conduct transactions or manage account activity instead of conducting business directly
examples: Friend withdraws funds on behalf of account holder
properties.required_action: Verify authority and beneficial ownership; document proxy relationship; escalate if unauthorized or suspicious

properties.description: Account receives a significant deposit but then shows no normal activity or usage patterns
properties.required_action: Monitor account; investigate source of funds and intended use; escalate if dormancy persists without explanation

properties.name: Large Deposit Followed by Third-Party Withdrawal

properties.description: Customer deposits a large sum immediately followed by withdrawal via a third party, suggesting potential money laundering or structuring
examples: Customer opens account, deposits £30,000, then has friend withdraw it
properties.required_action: Freeze account pending investigation; file SAR if suspicious activity confirmed; escalate immediately
